mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points month-over-month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to reduced output and lower earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals a tightening monetary policy with high inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with high inflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 month-over-month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200k MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a robust demand environment with a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% MoM and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp MoM
regime_hint: robust demand with strong labor market
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1%.
